Improve member benefits by enabling partner linkage and creating digital passes. Standardize the points
expiration process and boost performance with asynchronous processing of high volumes of data. Target
your audience better using unified individuals and set up data graphs in companion orgs.

  Get Added Benefits by Linking Your Loyalty Memberships
  Members can now link their membership with partner loyalty memberships to seamlessly access
  valuable co-branded rewards, such as personalized offers. Linking memberships provides members
  with additional benefits in the home loyalty program. For example, link a Marriott Bonvoy membership
  in the Uber app to earn Bonvoy points by taking an Uber ride. Members can use their iOS or Android
  mobile devices to link their loyalty program memberships from a partner’s app.
  Integrate Loyalty Programs Seamlessly with Google Wallet
  Drive customer engagement by integrating your loyalty program with Google Wallet. Members can
  create digital passes and conveniently access their full loyalty member profile on their mobile device.
  This ease of use encourages members to use their loyalty rewards and boosts program participation.
  Members can use their iOS or Android mobile devices to add their digital passes to the Google Wallet
  app.
  Global Promotions Management
  Increase customer cart size with volume-based promotions such as Buy 100 LevelX Batteries to Get
  10% Off on 20 Battery Testers. Reward customers with free products with easily relatable promotions
  such as Buy-One-Get-One-Free (BOGO). Show promotions to store employees, assisted sellers, and
  customers in their preferred languages. Run promotions on ecommerce sites powered by Experience


                                                   581
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                         Marketing


  Cloud. Assign permissions sets to users based on their roles. Create promotions for large product sets
  with ease. Find eligible promotions for items from across all their categories. Explain to customers and
  sellers why manually added coupons weren’t applied to carts.
  Boost Performance with Asynchronous Processing of High-Volume Redemption Transactions
  Process traceable redemption transactions asynchronously to handle high redemption volumes more
  effectively. Optimize batch processing of redemptions and currency sub-type roll-ups during
  traceability to improve performance and scalability.
  Optimize Point Accounting with Accurate Expiration of Points
  Use the Expire Fixed Non-Qualifying Points Using Aggregation Ledgers and Traceable Ledgers Data
  Processing Engine definition template to automate the precise expiration of fixed-type non-qualifying
  points. Ensure accurate point expiration by processing only points without pending traceability ledgers.
  The template leverages Aggregated Point Expiration Ledger records to calculate and expire points for
  members and currencies.
  Data 360 for Loyalty Management
  Enhance your audience targeting by using unified indvidual segments and improve data accuracy by
  setting up data graphs in companion orgs.
  Standardize Point Expiration by Using Current Date
  Standardize your point expiration processes by using real-time calculations with a capability to check
  whether the run date for a Data Processing Engine definition is in the future. The future run date is
  automatically replaced with the current date.
  Refine User Access with New Loyalty Management Permission Sets
  Update your user assignments with new permission sets to ensure that your admins and loyalty

  Do more with the new and updated Loyalty Management objects.

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available

• Expire Fixed Non-Qualifying Points
• Expire Activity Based Non-Qualifying Points
• Expire Fixed Non-Qualifying Points Using Aggregated Expiration Ledgers
• Expire Non-Qualifying Points Using Traceability Loyalty Ledgers
• Expire Fixed Non-Qualifying Points Using Aggregation Ledgers and Trace Ledgers
How: To get the latest updates, replace the existing Data Processing Engine definition templates with the
enhanced templates.

  MuleSoft API Catalog for Salesforce
  Manage and view your APIs and make them available to use in Salesforce. You can bring APIs into your

  practices for governance.

Automate UI Testing for Omniscripts and Flexcards

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Omnistudio now supports comprehensive UI testing for guided experiences and visual components by
using the UI Test Automation Model (UTAM) framework. UTAM improves deployment reliability by
validating end-to-end workflows. Write UI-driven tests for Omniscripts and Flexcards that validate full
user journeys exactly as they appear on screen. UTAM interacts directly with the interface to test user
inputs, navigation, actions, data rendering, and visual states.

Where: This change applies to Aura and LWR sites accessed through Lightning Experience in Enterprise,
Performance, and Unlimited editions where Omnistudio is enabled.

Who: This feature is available to Omnistudio customers who use the standard runtime and standard
designer.

Why: UTAM offers these key benefits:

• Abstracts Document Object Model (DOM) changes to keep UI tests stable, even when platform
    updates modify layouts.
• Simulates real user interactions across Omnscripts and Flexcards for end-to-end validation, from data
    entry to conditional logic.
•   Uses Page Object Model (POM) to organize reusable Page Objects (POs), simplifying test creation and
    maintenance.

How: To use UTAM for automated UI testing, first install and configure your preferred test runner (for
example, WebDriverIO or TestNG) to work with the UTAM framework. Next, leverage the Omnistudio
UTAM POs to create custom POs for your Omniscripts or Flexcards, abstracting common UI elements,
such as steps, inputs, and buttons. Then, build your test scripts on top of these custom POs by using
helper methods to launch the Omniscript, set field values, and perform navigation actions. Finally, verify
that the end-to-end user journey, validations, and element behaviors work as expected.

Salesforce Release Notes                                                                        Omnistudio

Accessibility Enhancements in Omnistudio

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available


                                                    606
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                       Omnistudio


until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Build inclusive user interfaces by using the accessibility enhancements in Flexcard and Omniscript
elements. These enhancements cover many accessibility requirements, such as enhanced screen reader
announcements, easier navigation, and a more powerful UI experience. Some enhancements are only
available when you turn on the Accessibility setting in the Flexcard and Omniscript designers. For
instance, this setting unlocks new properties for elements such as Radio, Radio Group, Block, and Data
Table. Other changes apply even without turning on this setting, such as new custom attributes for icons,
autocomplete options in several elements, and so on.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Experience Cloud sites, and all versions of
Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions where Omnistudio is enabled.

Who: This feature is available to Omnistudio customers who use the standard runtime. However,
changes under the Accessibility toggle apply to Omnistudio customers who use the standard runtime
and designer. All changes are available for the SLDS and SLDS+ themes.

Why: These enhancements make your components meet WCAG 2.2 web accessibility standards, helping
screen reader and keyboard-only users navigate your applications more effectively. Specific
improvements include:

• Improved Semantics: Navigate actions now use real links rather than placeholder links. Screen readers
    announce when links open in a new window.
•   Enhanced Navigation: Keyboard users can now access edit icons in Data Tables on focus. All actions
    support Space, Enter, and Escape keys.
•   Better Visual Feedback: Selected options in Multi-select and Radio elements now display a checkmark
    for clearer visual indication beyond color alone.

How: To access the optional enhancements, open your Flexcard or Omniscript in the standard designer,
select Setup, and enable the Accessibility toggle.

When you enable the Accessibility setting, these changes become available:

• Radio
   - Improved keyboard navigation
   - Support for new attributes: role=radiogroup , aria-required and aria-invalid
   - Image and color-pick radio buttons now show a visible checkmark when selected.
   - Users can use arrow keys to navigate color-pick options.
• Radio Group
   - The Set All checkbox now behaves correctly at runtime and can’t be unchecked once set.
   - When the focus is removed from a specific element, validation is triggered.
   - The DOM structure is updated for better accessibility.
• Block
   - Heading Level: You can now configure the heading level (H1-H6) for blocks to enforce a logical

                                                   607
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                        Omnistudio


       document structure.
     - Delete Confirmation: A confirmation prompt is available when deleting items in a block.
•   Data Table
     - Row Labels: Meaningful row labels for screen readers are now supported.
     - Action Buttons: Action buttons inside the table now have contextual labels.
     - Live Updates: Screen readers announce updates to the table content dynamically.
     - Keyboard Navigation: Improved navigation for edit icons and sort buttons (focus returns to the sort
       button after activation).
     - Loading Feedback: Screen readers now announce Loading states, for example, when a table is
       loading or refreshing.
•   Typeahead
     - An Edit Icon Label field is added so you can specify a name for the name of the edit icon. The
       default remains Edit, but you can customize the label as per your preference. This change is
      specific to the edit mode.
    - The option list container’s border maintains the minimum contrast ratio of 3:1 with its background
      color. This change is specific to SLDS Plus theme.
    - When the dropdown menu opens, focus is automatically set to the first selectable option. This
      change is specific to the Lookup mode.

• Action:
   - Navigate actions now announce when something opens in a new window.
   - Keyboard navigation is enhanced to mirror mouse click behavior.
   - New ARIA attributes are added for the Select Cards action. They announce checkbox actions such
      as selection, de-selection, and so on.

These improvements are available automatically without enabling the Accessibility toggle:

• Set as Disabled Property for Inputs: A new Set as disabled property is available for these elements, so
    that you can explicitly disable them on the pages that they’re used on.
     - Currency, Email, Number, Password, Range, Telephone, Text, Text Area, URL, and Lookup.
     - Checkbox: The Read-Only property is replaced by Set as disabled.
     - Multi-select: The Set as disabled property is added.
•   Select:
     - The default placeholder "-- No Value --" is changed to "Select a value".
     - Focus remains on the input while typing.
     - Value changes are reflected immediately.
     - The autocomplete input field is added.
•   Lookup:
     - With the new Clear Value option, you can clear the pre-selected value when the dropdown opens.
     - The autocomplete input field is added.
     - The search icon is removed from the runtime view.
• Icon:
   - Two new custom attributes are added, namely iconNameLeftAltText and
       iconNameRightAltText .
• - Telephone:

                                                    608
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                       Omnistudio


      - Visual contrast is improved for better readability.
   - Multi-Select:
     - Image multi-select options now display a visible checkmark.

Get Null Values Easily with the New Is Null Operator in Data
Mappers

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Use the new IS NULL operator in Omnistudio Data Mapper Extract and Turbo Extract to filter null or
empty records. Previously, the equality operator (=) didn’t consistently handle null filtering, often
requiring complex workarounds. For example, to get records with empty account IDs, a Data Mapper
operation such as AccountId = null AND Phone != null was required. With the IS NULL operator, you can
explicitly filter blank fields, without adding an additional condition, such as != null.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Experience Cloud sites, and all versions of
Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions where Omnistudio is enabled.

Who: This feature is available to Omnistudio customers who use the standard runtime and standard
designer.

optional child product, QuantumBit Essentials Training, when customers buy it as part of the bundle.

customers toward longer subscriptions of the bundled product and encourage purchases of the child

  Streamline Complex Quote Calculations with Smarter Price Propagation
  Manage complex, multi-level quotes by defining formulas that calculate and propagate discounts and
  totals throughout the quote hierarchy. Simplify pricing configuration for complex quote structures with
  up to 5 levels of nesting. Build consistent pricing flows by using ascending propagation to conditionally
  roll up totals and discounts to the parent level. Use horizontal calculations to compute values based
  on other fields within the same quote line or group.
  Package Your Pricing Workflow Seamlessly
  Migrate entire pricing solutions across Salesforce orgs by adding procedure plans directly to your
  deployment package. Transfer the complete execution flow of pricing and discovery procedures to
  reduce manual setup effort. Deploy your validated pricing workflow with speed and accuracy to ensure
  immediate consistency in every target org.
  Troubleshoot Pricing Elements with Advanced Price Log Settings
  Use Advanced Price Log Settings to collect detailed diagnostic data for complex pricing elements. The
  logs capture input values and complete exception details for elements such as Attribute-Based Price,
  Derived Price, and other logic-heavy elements. This framework streamlines troubleshooting and
  performance analysis so that admins can identify the root cause of issues.




                                                   624
Salesforce Release Notes                                                             Revenue Management


  Build Pricing Logic with Conditional IF Statements
  Solve complex pricing scenarios by using conditional IF statements and nested logic directly within the
  Formula-Based Pricing element. Pricing designers can now replicate complex business logic, such as
  intricate claculations for product pricing by using basis points or advanced logic for promotional
  discounts, without relying on custom code. This enhancement optimizes procedure readability and
  accelerates debugging.
  Accelerate Debugging of Pricing Flows
  Use auto-numbered steps and element descriptions in a pricing procedure to improve readability and
  provide a clear visual map of the execution path in the Pricing Operations Console. The numbering
  automatically adjusts when elements are added or moved, reducing manual effort and supporting
  faster, more accurate troubleshooting across pricing procedures.
  Pricing Operations Console Is Now Revenue Cloud Operations Console
  To better align with the data it presents, the Pricing Operations Console is now renamed to Revenue
  Cloud Operations Console. This change does not affect the console's functionality or user experience.

Updates in Default Product Configurator Flow

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions of Agentforce Revenue Management, formerly Revenue Cloud, with the Revenue
Cloud Growth or the Revenue Cloud Advanced license.

Why: Update your Configurator flow with the latest attributes so that new features work as expected and
you get a seamless configuration experience.

The ID of the transaction context for which the Configurator is launched
       Use the new Transaction Context ID attribute of the Input type on the Product Configurator
       Data Manager flow component.



                                                    633
Salesforce Release Notes                                                             Revenue Management


A boolean value that indicates whether to display the product attributes within the option card
       Use the new Display Option Card Attributes attribute of the Input type on the Product
       Configurator Option Groups flow component.


The number of product attributes to be displayed within the option card
      Use the new Option Card Attributes Limit attribute of the Input type on the Product
      Configurator Option Groups flow component.


A collection of Apex ProductConfig__Promotions records that contain the promotions eligible for
the product
        Use the new Eligible Promotions attribute. It's of Input type on the Product Configurator
        Summary flow component and of Output type on the Product Configurator Data Manager flow
        component.


A boolean value that indicates whether the messages component is fixed in position when scrolling
       Use the new Messages in Fixed Position attribute. It's of both Input and Output types on the
       Product Configurator Data Manager flow component, and of Input type on the Product
       Configurator Messages, Product Configurator Transaction Header, and Product Configurator
       Summary flow components.


A collection of Apex ProductConfig__Message records that contain alerts, warnings, and errors
encountered by the component
        Use the new Messages attribute of the Input type on the Product Configurator Transaction
        Header and Product Configurator Summary flow components.


A boolean value that indicates whether the section displaying price totals in the Summary
component is shown at run time
       Use the new Price Total Summary Section Visibility attribute. It's of Input type on the Product
       Configurator Summary flow component and of Output type on the Product Configurator Data
       Manager flow component.

This release is in preview

Manage complex deal structures easily by creating multiple ramp schedule groups, and amend ramped
and nonramped assets in a single transaction. Set up quote line import effortlessly in multicurrency orgs,
and automatically populate records related to imported quote lines. Handle transactions easily with
advanced filtering, automated and persistent line sorting, and faster instant pricing. Process amendment,
renewal, or cancellation transactions before the start date of an existing future-dated order.

  Autopopulate Default Child Lines and Attributes During Quote Line Import
  Speed up quoting and improve accuracy by using the new Data Processing Engine definition to
  autopopulate default records related to imported quote lines. When users import quote lines from
  CSV files, the import process populates default child lines for bundled products, and default quote
  line item attributes and their values. Users can also import static product bundles and products with
  static attributes.
  Set Up Quote Line Import Easily When Multiple Currencies Are Enabled
  Quickly configure quote line imports by using the new prebuilt Data Processing Engine definition
  template when your Salesforce org uses multiple currencies. This template reduces the manual setup
  steps previously required to add and map currency fields.
  Manage Complex Deals and Amendments by Using Multiple Ramp Schedule Groups
  Enable your users to create and manage multiple, independent ramp schedule groups on a single
  quote or order to handle complex deal structures. Users can also amend non-ramped and ramped
  assets—including ramped assets with different asset state period dates—in a single transaction. Sales
  reps can perform complex actions, such as “rip and replace,” to remove assets and add new ones in a
  single transaction.
  Enrich Navigation by Using Advanced Filtering
  Your sales reps and partners can now filter all quote and order lines including ramped lines, errored
  lines, and unconfigured lines by using predefined filters. They can also create advanced filters to target
  specific fields, operators, and values. They can manage complex transactions easily by applying filters
  across all groups or selected groups.
  Automate Consistent Line Item Sequencing on Quotes and Orders (Pilot)
  Sales reps can control how line items show up on quotes and orders by introducing an automated and
  persistent sort order. Line items now appear in the sequence in which they're added. Automatic Line
  Item Sequencing (pilot) maintains item order when converting a quote to an order, and resolves the
  unpredictable item order shuffling that previously occurred in processing. Sales reps can also manually
  reorder items, providing the reliable sequencing needed to adjust the order of items to meet specific
  business needs.
  Update Prices Faster by Using Instant Pricing
  Recalculate only the lines that have price-impacting changes on your quotes and orders. Give your
  sales reps faster and more accurate pricing results when they edit complex transactions.
  Show Precise Discounts in the Price Waterfall
  Show your sales reps discount percentages and amount adjustments in the price waterfall with the
  correct decimal precision. Percentage discounts show up to two decimal places, and amount
  adjustments follow the currency scale. Help sales reps understand discount values accurately and
  remove the confusion caused by rounded percentages.
  Speed Up Processing of Quotes and Orders with Context Reuse
  By preventing services from unnecessarily recreating context instances, this feature reduces wasted


                                                    635
Salesforce Release Notes                                                             Revenue Management


  resources, boosts efficiency, and prevents issues like stale data and race conditions. The context reuse
  feature improves the performance and responsiveness of Agentforce Revenue Management
  transactions by enabling components to share context. When sales reps handle quotes and orders,
  edits work smoothly, and data is uniform and up to date across all transaction editing workflows.
  Track Product Swap, Upgrade, and Downgrade Amendments
  Make sure that transactions are transparent and accurately track the intent of every sale change.
  Agentforce Revenue Management now natively supports Swaps, Upgrades, and Downgrades as
  distinct amendment types, which boosts the efficiency of your sales reps. New connections among the
  related quote line items, order items, and asset actions make sure that these transactions are
  recognizable and auditable. Sales reps save time and effort used in the previous method that simply
  recorded them as a cancellation and new product sale.

  sale. Your sales team can now perform all transaction amendment types, including adding, swapping,

  Gain more control over rate synchronization and ensure pricing consistency across transactions.

Advanced Approvals

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and

As an approval designer, use custom flow logic to auto-approve resubmitted records. Approve high-value
record requests faster by overriding approval conditions easily. Enhance your smart approval logic by
configuring step conditions with eight additional data types and up to 30 conditions for approval stage
and step criteria. Create detailed approval email templates for up to 8 different notification reasons,
giving reviewers all the necessary context to act on the request directly from their email.

  Approve Resubmissions Faster by Using Custom Logic
  Approval designers can now implement custom logic for auto-approving resubmitted records,
  overriding smart approval conditions. Make sure that urgent, high-value records move quickly through
  the approval process. Approval designers can create a custom flow to evaluate any necessary criteria,
  including checks against the prior submission details. Simplify this verification by using the new Get
  Previous Related Record Details invocable action within the flow to easily capture the previously
  submitted record's details. The new Use Custom Auto Approval Logic field on the approval step then
  stores the custom flow’s decision value to determine if the step is auto-approved.
  Improve Approval Reviews with Custom Email Templates for Key Approval Paths
  Give approval designers the ability to use Lightning or Visualforce email templates. Designers can
  associate these templates with specific approval steps or the entire workflow. They can configure these
  templates for up to 8 different notification reasons that are relevant to approval submitters and
  reviewers. Previously, the custom email templates configured within the approval workflow lacked
  advanced formatting capabilities and didn’t support custom submitter emails. Use the new templates
  to show complex record data in structured formats, such as tables and images, so that your approval
  reviewers have all the necessary context to act on the requests directly from their email.
  Process Smart Approvals Faster by Skipping Condition Checks
  Give approval designers the option to skip the evaluation of the entry conditions in an approval step
  within a smart approval process. Help them save approval processing time by skipping unnecessary
  condition checks from resubmission evaluation based on your workflow’s context. For instance, if the
  submitted record description is empty during resubmission, designers can skip the condition if it’s


                                                   645
Salesforce Release Notes                                                             Revenue Management


  irrelevant to the evaluation.
  Define Complex Smart Approval Logic with More Data Types
  Configure the approval step entry conditions in an approval workflow by using nine additional data
  types, such as Date Time, Boolean, and Currency. Previously, you could define conditions for only the
  Text and Number data types. Help approval designers build complex and precise smart approval logic
  that aligns closely with your business rules, and reduce manual review time. For example, set a Date
  step entry condition that requires an approval step during resubmission only if the resubmission date
  is after a certain date.
  Manage Complex Workflows Easily by Adding More Conditions
  Define up to 30 conditions for an approval stage exit, approval step entry, and approval step exit in an
  approval workflow. Previously, you defined a maximum of 10 conditions. Give approval designers the
  flexibility to build workflows that manage complex approval requests and minimize manual reviews for
  their users.

  Store and access more data with these new Advanced Approvals objects and changes to existing
  Advanced Approvals objects.

Billing Amendments

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available

Maintain accurate billing schedules during rollbacks, term or price changes, product swaps, and line-level
date updates. Align billing schedules with changes to future-dated orders and quotes, and generate
precise billing for multiple ramp deals.

  Align Billing Dates with Order Item Detail and Quote Line Detail Records
  Get precise billing for orders and quotes that have multiple start and end periods. Billing prioritizes the
  start and end dates found on Quote Line Detail and Order Item Detail records. If no dates are
  specified on the detail records, then Billing uses the dates from the parent order or quote item.
  Align Billing with Subscription Term Updates
  Generate precise billing schedules automatically when your customer extends or shortens a
  subscription term during an amendment. Keep billing in sync with revised contractual terms by
  aligning billing schedules with the updated start and end dates on the order product.
  Align Billing with Changes to Future-Dated Orders and Quotes
  Support dynamic customer needs by processing billing for amendments and renewals that occur
  before a scheduled future-dated order or quote. Get accurate billing schedules for the amended or
  renewed assets under termed, evergreen, and one-time products. Ensure alignment with future billing
  periods and eliminate the need for manual reconciliation.
  Capture Accurate Billable Amounts After Rollbacks
  Update billing schedules automatically when customers roll back a future-dated amendment, renewal,
  or cancellation. The rollback adds adjusting billing schedules to negate the previous change, ensuring
  that the schedule shows the correct view of what to bill next. Maintain accurate billing and a clean,
  reliable schedule history without manual corrections.
  Generate Precise Billing for Multiple Ramp Deals
  Extend group ramps to support multiple billing schedules with accuracy and consistency. For each
  product ramp ID in a ramp deal, Billing creates a billing schedule group. For every segment in the



                                                    667
Salesforce Release Notes                                                               Revenue Management


  product ramp schedule, Billing creates a billing schedule in the billing schedule group to represent the
  group’s ramping and timeline. Support accurate billing for independent ramp schedule groups across
  mixed asset types while keeping multi-asset amendments consistent.
  Maintain Billing Accuracy During Price Changes
  Automatically update billing amounts to reflect any changes in product pricing. Generate accurate
  billing schedules and invoices that capture any increase or decrease in the prices of termed, evergreen,
  or one-time product subscriptions.
  Ensure Billing Accuracy During Product Swaps
  Ensure billing accuracy when you swap one-time, evergreen, termed, and bundled products. Get auto-
  generated billing schedules for the products that are swapped out and swapped in.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and

Who: To recover and void credit memos, you need the Billing Admin, the Billing Operations User, or the
Credit Memo Operations User permission set.

How: To recover credit memos, from the App Launcher, find and select Credit Memos. Open a credit
memo in the pending or error state. Then click Recover Credit Memo. For credit memos with tax, the
action creates a debit memo and voids the credit memo. For credit memos with no tax, the action
simply cancels the credit memo.

To void a posted credit memo, open the credit memo record and click Void Credit Memo.

and Functional Currencies.

Salesforce Contracts

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Contract authors and template designers have greater control over how they structure, style, and review
contract content. Improvements to section behavior, clause formatting, and profile-based access help
maintain consistent layouts, protect sensitive content, and make sure that the intended users participate
in internal reviews. Expanded reconciliation and token capabilities keep data accurate across contracts,
line items, and related records. Large and complex documents are more responsive during editing,
comparison, and check-in. Document Template migration improvements further preserve document
structure and clause relationships as they move between Salesforce orgs.

  Control Section Name Visibility When Inserting Content
  Template designers and contract authors can choose whether a section name appears in the
  generated document. Previously, section name always appeared. They can now delete section names
  in the Microsoft 365 editor when they don’t want it to appear in the generated document. The section
  name remains visible under the Section tab in the Microsoft 365 add-in panel to manage section
  content.
  Preserve Formatting When Inserting Clauses
  Clauses now retain their defined indentation, line spacing, lists, fonts, and other rich text formatting



                                                    695
Salesforce Release Notes                                                              Revenue Management


  defined in the clause library when inserted into a document. Previously, inserting clauses into a
  Microsoft 365 template and contract document caused the document styles to override the clause’s
  original formatting.
  Assign Profile-Based Access for Sections
  Control who can update sensitive content, including token values, by limiting section-level access to
  specific profiles. During template creation, the designer can select which profiles can edit a section for
  contract authoring and internal review.
  Control Internal Reviewers Based on Users or Profiles
  Contract authors can choose between a user-based or profile-based mode when initiating internal
  reviews. Prevent unintended edits and keep review activities focused on the appropriate participants.
  Reconcile More Data with Expanded Data True-Up Capacity
  The Microsoft 365 Word Data True-Up feature now handles more than 200 field tokens and includes
  support for line item tokens, improving reconciliation across contract fields and detailed line item
  values. Data True-Up also supports reconciling data sourced from related records, such as quotes and
  opportunities.
  Review Redline Differences in a Comparison Document
  Get full visibility of changes when reviewing contract versions. You can generate a comparison
  document that highlights added, edited, and deleted content relative to the base version. This
  enhancement makes it easier to understand changes introduced during redlining across contract
  document versions.
  Improve Document Accuracy with Advanced Data True-Up Enhancements
  Data True-Up token processing now supports nested object structures and reference fields up to one
  level, including related objects, such as opportunities and quotes. You can pull token values from
  related records rather than only from contracts, improving reconciliation accuracy for complex data.
  Support for reference fields on custom objects also helps keep contract data aligned with information
  stored across your data model.
  Migrate Templates Across Salesforce Environments
  Move Microsoft 365 document templates between Salesforce orgs while preserving clause references
  and section-level access controls. For example, move templates from a sandbox to a production org.
  This process helps maintain template integrity across orgs and environments. Before migrating
  templates, use a data migration tool to transfer the clause records, clause versions, and profile data to
  the target org. After you migrate the template, the built-in key mapping aligns the clause and profile
  references with the corresponding clause records in the target org.
  Manage Document Check-In Behavior with Configurable Async Processing
  Reduce latency and timeouts when checking in large documents with asynchronous processing.
  Check-in occurs asynchronously when a document contains more than 200 doc elements, such as
  sections, clauses, and tokens in the Microsoft 365 document. Async check-in is enabled by default, but
  you can disable it to make all check-ins run synchronously.
  Find Content in Sections and Clauses Faster
  Contract authors can navigate large documents more easily with the new search field on the Sections
  and Standalone Clauses tabs of the Microsoft 365 add-in. The search results update with each
  keystroke and show only matching items in the panel, helping you locate the right content quickly
  without manual scrolling. Search also expands collapsed sections when it finds relevant results.



                                                    696
Salesforce Release Notes                                                             Revenue Management


  Changed Connect REST API Request Bodies in Salesforce Contracts
  The Content Link Load and Data Sync APIs include enhancements to reduce multiple per-field queries
  into a single grouped fetch request for improved performance.

                                                   697
Salesforce Release Notes                                                               Revenue Management


during template designing and contract editing, leading to inconsistent clause presentation. This
enhancement preserves clause formatting unless authors or designers intentionally change it, reducing

Salesforce Document Generation

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Generate clearer documents with precise data by applying data filters, transformation logic, and richer
token coverage. These updates help make sure that structured content, nested values, and line item
details are present accurately. Generate large documents more efficiently, even when they include
substantial content or complex formatting. Achieve consistent in-browser previews by using the hybrid
file handling setting. Remove interim previews in Omniscripts to keep only the final version and reduce
storage use.

  Filter Context Data for Document Generation
  Apply a context filter in the template designer so that generated documents include only the data that
  meets your criteria. Select from predefined filters that support up to 5 conditions to fetch precise and
  relevant data from your context definitions. Adding a filter at design time avoids extra inputs, reduces
  errors, and delivers consistent and high-quality document output. For example, filter order items to
  include only products priced above a certain threshold, and sort them by quantity so that the
  generated document highlights the most relevant items. Document Generation in the Omnistudio
  managed package doesn’t support Context Service.
  Transform Context Data Before Generating Documents
  Generate documents with clean, standardized, and business-ready data content by transforming the
  context data using the sample Apex plug-in. Run the Apex plug-in after context hydration to adjust
  formatting, grouping, string manipulation, token value changes, and other lightweight changes to
  meet business needs. This capability enables advanced transformation logic for scenarios that filtering
  alone can’t address. For example, transform flat line items into a bundle with child products so that
  the document shows each bundle with its related components. You can also group line items by
  category or region so that the document presents organized sections with related items together.
  Document Generation in the Omnistudio managed package doesn’t support this Apex plug-in.



                                                   704
Salesforce Release Notes                                                             Revenue Management


  Generate Larger Documents with Expanded File Size Support
  Scale document generation to support larger outputs, generating single PDF, DOCX, or PPTX files up to
  200 MB. This enhancement enables high-volume, media-rich, and evidence-heavy use cases and helps
  you generate complete documents in one pass without splitting content or assembling files outside
  Salesforce.
  Preview Documents by Using Hybrid Setting Across Contracts and Omniscripts
  The PDF document previewer provides secure in-browser previewing when you configure Salesforce
  file upload and download security settings. The PDF previewer now works with the hybrid file handling
  setting instead of relying only on the execute-in-browser option. The hybrid file handling setting
  improves preview consistency across browsers and Experience Cloud sites.
  Manage Preview Document Storage in Omniscripts
  Document reviews often involve regenerating the preview several times, resulting in multiple stored
  files and increased storage consumption. You can now easily discard intermediate previews by clicking
  the delete icon in Omniscripts to keep only the final version, reducing costs and achieving storage
  organization.

Refine your territory design in densely populated areas by allowing a single boundary, such as a postal
code, to be assigned to multiple sales areas. This new capability is supported only for live data
alignments and gives you more customization when modeling complex geographic territories like New
York City or London. Units, however, can still only be assigned to a single area. Utilize area-level

                                                    737
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                               Sales


How: Admins and users can enable overlapping boundaries through several methods in the boundary
legend. To use the new Assign to Multiple Areas action, select boundaries, choose the action, select
multiple areas from the picklist, then select Preview and Confirm your changes. Alternatively, you can
inline edit the assignment field in the boundary legend by selecting multiple areas from the list of area
names.




To modify overlapping areas independently or to enable optimization (which is disabled when
overlapping boundaries are in focus), use the Set Focus action to temporarily remove overlapping areas
from the map. Boundaries that overlap are denoted by a hexagonal "honeycomb" pattern on the map
and in the boundary legend.

Allocate Financial Targets to Accounts in Territory Planning

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Distribute top-down financial targets directly to accounts within Territory Planning. You can split targets
evenly, weight them based on criteria like annual revenue, or distribute by defined segments. To ensure
realistic planning, the allocation logic respects existing bottom-up targets set by the field. This alignment
simplifies the transition from territory design to quota planning.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Professional, Enterprise,
Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions with Web Services API enabled.

How: Configure a goal within an alignment connected to a segment data source to enable allocation
options. Use an allocation formula to distribute targets using even, weighted, or bucketed methods,
while automatically subtracting any existing bottom-up targets from the total. You can also import
overrides or publish targets to use them in downstream quota planning.

Create Alignment-Based Quota Plans

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Streamline the planning process by creating quota plans directly from existing territory alignments.
Planners can now view account-level details and metadata within the quota planning interface to inform
target setting. Because the plans share data, updates to territory models flow into the quota plan,
ensuring assignments and targets remain synchronized.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Professional, Enterprise,
Unlimited, and Developer editions with Sales Planning in English only and with Web Services API
enabled.

Why: Planning traditionally relies on assumptions that shift rapidly as deals close or account rosters
change, which can force teams back into planning cycles. By linking quota plans to territory alignments,
Sales Operations can maintain control over data updates while validating plans against the latest
hierarchy and assignment structures. This integration provides visibility into account-specific metadata,
such as historical revenue, helping to balance quotas fairly even when territory structures are complex or
shifting.



                                                    740
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                             Sales


How: Select a territory alignment when creating a new quota plan to import the area hierarchy and
account data. The hierarchy remains read-only within the quota plan to preserve the territory structure,
but you can view account details and allocate targets based on the imported areas. If the source territory
changes, such as a deleted area, the system flags the mismatch and prompts you to accept changes to
keep the plans aligned.

Adopt Authorized Email Domains (Release Update)

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability



                                                   742
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                              Sales


within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

If you previously worked with Salesforce Customer Support to disable email change verifications, set up
authorized email domains instead. Salesforce is retiring the existing exemption process for disabling this
feature, and authorized email domains provide the same benefit. This update is available starting in
Spring ’26.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Salesforce Classic, and the Salesforce mobile app in
all editions.

When: Salesforce enforces this update in Winter ’27. To get the major release upgrade date for your
instance, go to Trust Status, search for your My Domain name or instance, and click the maintenance tab.

Why: The process to disable email change verification relied on a manual change by Salesforce Customer
Support, which created operational inefficiencies and potential risks. With authorized email domains,
you simplify the onboarding process for new users by using domain-level email verification. Email
verification is bypassed for users with email addresses on a domain that you trust.


     Note These changes relate to the verification of email addresses stored in Salesforce and the ability
     to send email from Salesforce. There’s no change to the requirements for account verification for
     access to Salesforce.


How: To review this update, from Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and then
select Release Updates. For Adopt Authorized Email Domains, follow the testing and activation steps.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Authorize a Domain for Return Email Verification
  Knowledge Article: Disable 'Email Change Verification'

Migrate Microsoft 365 Authentication in Einstein Activity Capture to Microsoft Graph

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability

Transition your Einstein Activity Capture’s Microsoft 365 authentication from Exchange Web Services
(EWS) to Microsoft Graph, which is more modern, secure, and scalable. Microsoft is retiring EWS in
October 2026, so switch to Microsoft Graph to avoid service disruption. Proactive notifications and a
single-click tool make the migration process smooth.

Where: This feature is available in Lightning Experience in Starter, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
Einstein 1 Sales, and Agentforce 1 Sales editions. It’s also available with the Einstein for Sales, Sales
Engagement, and Revenue Intelligence add-ons.

When: This feature is available starting in February 2026.



                                                    744
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                                    Sales


Who: The update is available if Einstein Activity Capture is configured to use Microsoft 365. If you’re
setting up Einstein Activity Capture with Microsoft 365 starting in Spring ’26, you’re automatically
authenticated by using Microsoft Graph.

Why: This migration is essential to align with Microsoft’s evolving security standards and to avoid
potential disruptions as EWS reaches its end of life in October 2026. By transitioning to Microsoft Graph,
Salesforce makes sure that your organization remains compliant and competitive, with improved support
for modern features and enhanced user-level authentication.

How: Before and during migration, make sure that your Azure admin has granted Microsoft Graph
consent. Then, use the single-click migration tool to complete the migration and select the correct
authentication method.




If Einstein Activity Capture is configured to use User-Level OAuth, users must reconnect to their Microsoft
365 accounts to complete the connection migration.

Make Captured Emails Available as Activity Data by Updating Einstein Activity Capture

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Use an option in Setup to update Einstein Activity Capture and migrate previously captured email to



                                                   747
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                                  Sales


Salesforce activity data. With this update and migration, all new email data and previously captured
email data are synced, stored, and available as activity data. This update and migration makes email data
available to platform tools and operations. After you start the update and migration process, it runs and
is completed automatically.

Where: This feature is available in Lightning Experience in Starter, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
Einstein 1 Sales, and Agentforce 1 Sales editions. It’s also available with the Einstein for Sales, Sales
Engagement, and Revenue Intelligence add-ons.

When: This tool rolls out as a staggered release beginning late December 2025 in sandboxes and early
2026 in production.

Who: This is available if Einstein Activity Capture is set up without Sync Email as Salesforce Activity. If
you’ve set up Sync Email as Salesforce Activity, you don’t need to update or migrate.

Why: Updating Einstein Activity Capture turns on Sync Email as Salesforce Activity for all newly captured
email and migrates previously captured email to activity data. Email synced as activity data is stored in
EmailMessage and Task object records, making it available to platform reports, automation, and APIs. It
also offers more granular privacy and sharing settings for captured email data. Previously, captured email
data wasn’t stored in standard objects or available to platform tools and required unique reports to
access and analyze the data. Sync Email as Salesforce Activity was introduced as a default setting for
Einstein Activity Capture in Summer ’25.

  actionable output, enabling automation of document-based workflows. Organizations get lots of
  unstructured and semistructured documents that have important business data. But getting and
  processing this information by hand is time-consuming and can introduce mistakes. With MuleSoft for
  Flow: IDP you define what data to extract through custom configurations. You set confidence
  thresholds for automatic processing, and route low-confidence results for human review to verify
  accuracy. Manage your document processing configurations on the Document Processing tab in the
  Automation app.

Open Screen Flows in Lightning Experience with a URL (Generally Available)

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Launch screen flows in Lightning Experience and Lightning console apps with a new standardized URL
format. Opening flows in Lightning has several benefits, such as faster performance, keeping your users
in Lightning console apps, and providing a more consistent browser experience. You can also pass
information into your flow through its URL. The new URL format also supports the Salesforce Cosmos
theme, and flow local actions.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Essentials, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
and Developer editions.



                                                   783
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                   Salesforce Flow


How: To open a flow in Lightning Experience, append /lightning/flow/YourFlowNameHere to your
URL. To run a specific flow version, append /lightning/flow/YourFlowNameHere/versionId to
your URL. Flows that open in Lightning Experience have improved performance because most required
Lightning components are already loaded into the browser session. In Lightning console apps, your tabs
are preserved when a flow opens, and you can switch to other tabs while the flow is working. Using the
new URL format also ensures that your browser behaves consistently, with forward, back, and your
browser history working as expected.

To pass data into a flow through its URL, append ?flow__variableIdHere=value to the end of your URL.
For example, to pass a case number into a flow, /lightning/flow/
YourFlowNameHere?flow__variableIdHereID={!Case.CaseNumber} .

Use & to append multiple variables into a flow. For example, /lightning/flow/
YourFlowNameHere?flow__varUserFirst={!$User.FirstName}&flow__varUserLast={!$User.LastName}
passes both the user first name and last name into the flow.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Choosing Between Lightning and Non-Lightning Flow URL Formats (can be outdated
  or unavailable during release preview)
  Salesforce Help: Customize a Flow URL to Control Finish Behavior (can be outdated or unavailable
  during release preview)
  Salesforce Help: Send Variable Values to a Flow Using the Flow's URL (can be outdated or unavailable
  during release preview)

  In activation-triggered flows, to include data from the activation in the Send Email Message action, use
  the $ActivationData variable in the email.
  Run Segment-Triggered Flows at The Right Time with More Scheduling Options
  Run segment-triggered flows on customizable schedules for more control and precision. For example,
  run a flow every hour to ensure you're working with the latest data, or schedule flows to run only on
  weekdays to avoid weekend sends. New scheduling options include Hourly, Daily on Weekdays,
  Weekly on specific days, Monthly on specific days, and Yearly.
  Get More Targeted Segments in Segment-Triggered Flows
  Create segment-triggered flows with segments built on Individual data model object (DMO) and
  engagement records, not just a Unified Individual DMO. For example, create a segment of all contacts
  converted yesterday. This update enables more precise targeting and provides access to engagement-
  specific data like order details or registration information.
  Test Multiple Records in Segment-Triggered Flows in Debug
  Test up to 10 records simultaneously. Use the debug panel to instantly verify how different customers
  move through your flow. This update helps you quickly identify issues across diverse customer profiles
  before activation.
  Trigger Automation Event-Triggered Flows When CRM Records Change
  Now you can trigger an automation event-triggered flow when a prospect, lead, or contact record
  changes, or when a record related to a prospect, lead, or contact record changes. For example, send a
  personalized email to a contact when a case is closed, or trigger a follow-up flow that notifies a lead
  owner when an opportunity moves to a new stage. This update helps you engage customers
  immediately when key business events occur, with prospect, lead, or contact data available for
  personalization in your messages.
  Stay Informed About Path Experiment Outcomes
  Users who activate flows now receive automatic in-app notifications when path experiments are
  completed. Notifications cover winner selection, fallback handling, and inconclusive outcomes. This
  change keeps flow creators informed without requiring additional setup. If the activating user is
  deactivated, no notification is sent.
  View Path Comparison Analytics in Path Experiment Element
  Monitor path experiment results without leaving the Flow Builder canvas. The new Analytics tab in the
  Path Experiment element panel shows total participants, metrics, and confidence levels for path
  comparison. Monitor experiment results at a glance with this embedded summary, which is consistent
  with analytics available in other flow elements. To see in-depth analytics, click View Analytics.
  Control Path Selection When Debugging Path Experiments
  Configure the Path Experiment element to randomize path assignment or manually select a winning
  path while debugging. Randomization is the default, but you can validate specific paths without
  relying on chance by using manual selection. With the manual selection configuration, you can test
  the exact path you want to validate.

Salesforce Release Notes                                                                    Salesforce Flow


  View Path Experiment History
  Understand what happened during your path experiments with the new History tab. View all changes
  since activation, including timestamps, who made changes, and whether actions were automated or
  manual. Track events like experiment start, winner selection, delayed group releases, and fallback
  handling.
  Trace Individual Paths Through Flows with View Flow Run for Individual
  Troubleshoot specific customer issues by viewing the exact execution path that an individual took
  through a flow run. This capability shows you which branching paths were followed, what elements
  were completed, and where the individual potentially encountered errors or delays. This detailed view
  helps administrators investigate specific customer complaints, verify personalization logic, and identify
  bottlenecks for specific contacts in your marketing automation flows.

  Remove Individuals from Flows Externally via API
  Remove individuals from flows when external systems trigger exits via API. For example, exit
  customers from flows when they complete an order or when they reach a specified status. This update

Use Decisions, Add Exit Rules, and More with Enhancements to Activation-Triggered
Flows

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

In activation-triggered flows, you can now use the Decision element, add exit and reentry conditions,
pause an active flow, and in the Transform element, map activation data up to 5 levels deep.

Where: This change applies to Data 360 in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.
Activation-triggered flows are also available for Marketing Cloud Growth and Marketing Cloud Advanced
editions with Data 360.

How: To add exit rules and set reentry conditions, edit the flow’s Start element. You can reference the
$ActivationData system variable to set exit rules based on the activation. To set reentry conditions, select
a value for the Can Rejoin Flow field. Always is the default value and means an individual can reenter a
flow before they exit. After completion means individuals can enter a flow only after they exit it. Never
means that an individual can’t enter the flow again.

To pause an active flow, click the Pause button in the button bar. The button changes to a Resume
button when paused. When a flow is paused, processing stops at each element and its people and data
are held until you resume the flow. After you resume the flow, everything that was held is processed at
one time and then the flow continues as usual.

  Salesforce Help: Create an Activation-Triggered Flow (can be outdated or unavailable during release
  preview)

Assign Flow Tests to Specific Flow Versions for More Control

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally

Reuse tests from previous flow versions if the scenario still applies to a new version. Align flow tests
precisely with each flow version so updates don’t cause incorrect results from other flow versions.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Professional, Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited,
and Developer editions.



                                                     800
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                       Salesforce Flow


Why: Previously, a flow test applied only to the latest flow version. You deleted previous tests that didn’t
apply to the new flow version. For example, you deleted the flow test for flow version 1 after creating the
flow test for flow version 2. Starting in Spring ’26, you associate the same test with multiple flow versions.
Decide which test scenario is for which flow version. When you save a new flow version, the system
automatically includes tests from the source flow version.

How: From Flow Builder, open a record-triggered flow and create a flow test. Complete the test details.
Then select the flow versions that you want to associate with the test.

The flow test runs for the selected flow versions.

Flow and Process Run-Time Changes in API Version 66.0

This release is in preview

within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally

These updates affect only flows and processes that are configured to run on API version 66.0 or later.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Salesforce Classic, and all versions of the mobile
app in Essentials, Professional, Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

How: With versioned updates you can test and adopt run-time behavior changes for individual flows and
processes at your convenience. To change the run-time API version of a flow, open it in Flow Builder and
edit the flow version properties. To change the run-time API version of a process, open it in Process
Builder and edit its properties.

Enforce No-Argument Constructor on Apex Classes
       With this versioned update, you can access certain built-in Apex classes that are available to be
       used as invocable action parameters. This versioned update enforces no-argument constructor
        visibility of all Apex classes, including the invocableVariable Apex class. Public no-argument
        constructors in managed packages are visible only when the access code is in the same package.
        An Apex action that refers to a non-visible no-argument constructor invocableVariable
        Apex class results in errors.


Record-Triggered Flows Issue with Non-Insertable Fields Was Fixed
       Record-triggered flows that run before records are saved now respect the internal writeable
       status of non-insertable fields. If existing flows try to update fields that aren’t editable, this error
       message appears: Invalid target field for field update.

Enforcing No-Argument Constructor on Apex Classes Used for Invocable Action

When this update is enabled, you get access to certain built-in Apex classes that are available to be used
as invocable action parameters. Additionally, this update enforces the visibility of the no-argument
constructor on any class. This update was scheduled to be enforced in Summer ’26. Starting in Spring
’26, Salesforce no longer enforces this update, but we recommend that you enable it. This release
update was previously named Enforce Permission Requirements Defined on Built-In Apex Classes Used
as Inputs.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in
Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

When: This update was scheduled to be enforced in Summer ’26. Starting Spring ’26, Salesforce no
longer enforces this update.

How: When you enable this update, built-in Apex classes that were unavailable become available for
Apex actions. Because of this change, the visibility of the no-argument constructor for the
invocableVariable Apex class is also enforced. Public no-argument constructors in managed
packages are no longer visible unless the access code is in the same package. An Apex action that refers
to a non-visible no-argument constructor invocableVariable Apex class results in errors.

From Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and then select Release Updates. To get
the Enforcing No-Argument Constructor on Apex Classes Used for Invocable Action Parameters release
update, follow the testing and activation steps.


Sort Apex Batch Action Results by Request Order (Release Update)

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available

Salesforce Release Notes                                                                        Salesforce Flow

With this update enabled, Apex batch action results are shown in the order that the requests are
received. Currently, error-prone requests are prioritized at the top of the result list, and successful
requests are at the bottom.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Enterprise, Performance,
Unlimited, and Developer editions.

When: Salesforce enforces this update in Summer ’26. To get the major release upgrade date for your
instance, go to Trust Status, search for your instance, and click the maintenance tab.

Why: Currently, error-prone requests are prioritized at the top of the result list, and successful requests
are at the bottom. With this change, action results are shown in the order that the requests are received.

How: After this update is applied, Apex batch action results are shown in the order that the requests are
received. Then, from Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and then select Release
Updates. To get the Sort Apex Batch Action Results by Request Order release update, follow the testing
and activation steps.

Other Changes to Flow Approval Processes

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Learn about improvements to Flow Approval Processes.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, all Einstein 1,
and Developer editions.

Why: Flow approval process designers can now:

• Provide input values and setup options one time per Flow Builder session instead of for every flow
    approval process debug run. Flow Builder preserves debug data such as triggering record inputs,
    debug options, and input variable values when you switch between Edit mode and Debug mode.
    Refreshing your browser or closing Flow Builder clears all debug settings.
•   Reduce email volume from approval work item notifications for individuals up the role hierarchy by
    using the new Send approval work item emails only to queue members setting. This approval setting
    limits notifications for queue-assigned approval steps to only queue members and their delegates. The
    setting has no effect if role hierarchy isn’t enabled.
•   Use the Step panel’s Configure Test Output tab, previously known as Debug Configuration, to set test
    output values. The Manually Set Output Values option is now labeled Use Test Output. The new
    terminology reinforces that you’re specifying test values to use instead of running actual steps. All
    functionality remains the same.
•   Place the Orchestration Work Guide, renamed from Flow Orchestration Work Guide, on the record
    page of an approval step’s related record in Experience Builder.
•   Use the updated options in the Decision Logic section of the Decision element. See Decision Logic
    Labels Were Updated for Clarity.

Other Changes to Flow Orchestration

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available

where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability

Learn about improvements to Flow Orchestration.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions.

Why: Orchestration designers can now:

• Provide input values and setup options one time per Flow Builder session instead of for every
    orchestration debug run. Flow Builder preserves debug data such as triggering record inputs, debug
    options, and input variable values when you switch between Edit mode and Debug mode. Refreshing
    your browser or closing Flow Builder clears all debug settings.
•   Reduce email volume from orchestration work item notifications for individuals up the role hierarchy.
    The new Send orchestration work item queue emails only to queue members setting in Process
    Automation Settings limits notifications for queue-assigned interactive steps to only queue members.
    The setting has no effect if role hierarchy isn’t enabled.
•   Use the Step panel’s Configure Test Output tab, previously known as Debug Configuration, to set test
    output values. The Manually Set Output Values option is now labeled Use Test Output. The new
    terminology reinforces that you’re specifying test values to use instead of running actual steps. All
    functionality remains the same.
•   Place the Orchestration Work Guide, renamed from Flow Orchestration Work Guide, on the record
    page of an interactive step’s related record in Experience Builder.
•   Use the updated options in the Decision Logic section of the Decision element. See Decision Logic
    Labels Were Updated for Clarity.

Extract Data from Digital and Scanned Documents by Using
MuleSoft for Flow: IDP (Generally Available)

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Use MuleSoft for Flow: IDP to transform unstructured and semistructured data into structured,
actionable output, enabling automation of document-based workflows. Organizations get lots of
unstructured and semistructured documents that have important business data. But getting and
processing this information by hand is time-consuming and can introduce mistakes. With MuleSoft for
Flow: IDP you define what data to extract through custom configurations. You set confidence thresholds
for automatic processing, and route low-confidence results for human review to verify accuracy. Manage
your document processing configurations on the Document Processing tab in the Automation app.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Professional (with API
access add-on), Performance, Enterprise, and Unlimited editions. Document processing configurations
can be edited or deleted only in the Automation app. Requires the MuleSoft for Flow: IDP add-on
license, which is available in multiple offerings.

How: Define the data fields and tables you want to extract from documents by creating a document
processing configuration in the Automation Lightning app. Build the human review workflow by creating
an orchestration that routes documents with low confidence scores to a screen flow for a user to
manually review and continue the process. To process documents uploaded to Salesforce, in Flow
Builder, add an Extract Data from Document action to a flow or an orchestration and select the
Document ID and Document Processing Configuration to reference.

A Warning Was Added for Potential Custom Domain Disruption

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

If your custom domain can experience disruption when you move to Salesforce Edge Network, you see a
warning on the My Domain Setup page.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Enterprise, Performance,
and Unlimited editions.

Why: A custom domain serves your site content on a domain that you own, such as
https://www.example.com. When a third-party service or content delivery network (CDN) hosts a
custom domain, the target host name for that domain changes when your org moves to Salesforce Edge
Network. Until your third-party service or CDN updates that value, your custom domain stops working.

To reduce the risk of outages during the move to Salesforce Edge Network, we added a warning on the



                                                   830
Salesforce Release Notes                                                             Security, Identity, and Privacy


My Domain page when you edit the Routing and Policies section. If your org isn’t on Salesforce Edge
Network and a third party serves at least one of the custom domains in the org, you see this warning.




How: If you see this warning, coordinate with your third-party service or CDN to update the target host
name for your custom domain as part of your move to Salesforce Edge Network.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Considerations for Custom Domains That Use a Third-Party Service or CDN (can be
  outdated or unavailable during release preview)
  Salesforce Help: Salesforce Edge Network (can be outdated or unavailable during release preview)
