Track Attempts to Use Uninstalled Connected Apps

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

You can now track denied attempts to use connected apps that aren't installed in your org (uninstalled
apps for short). By tracking these denied attempts, you can identify both legitimate and suspicious
attempts to use uninstalled apps. You can decide whether to allow usage of the app or to block it
entirely.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in all
editions.




                                                    835
Salesforce Release Notes                                                        Security, Identity, and Privacy


Why: To prevent unauthorized access to your data, Salesforce automatically denies attempts to use
uninstalled connected apps unless a user has the Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps user permission.
This user permission is intended only for highly trusted users, like admins. As a result, non-admin users
can be blocked from using uninstalled apps that have legitimate use cases. Now that you can track
denied attempts, you can easily see when a user is stuck in this situation. To allow these users to access
legitimate apps from trusted developers, install these apps.

By tracking denied attempts, you can also see if a threat actor is trying to use connected apps to get
access to your org. To tighten security, block suspicious apps. Blocking a connected app ends all sessions
and prevents further usage, even for users with the Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps user
permission.

How: On the Connected Apps OAuth Usage page in Setup, review the Denied Attempts Due to Usage
Restriction column. You can also review the date and time of the most recent denied attempt.

Set Up Passwordless Login with Passkeys (Beta)

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Give users a fast, easy, and phishing-resistant alternative to passwords. You can now enable passwordless
login with passkeys. With this feature, users can log in with a built-in authenticator (such as Touch ID or
Face ID) or a security key (such as a YubiKey or mobile device). Look forward to fewer password resets,
fewer login issues, and happier users.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in all
editions.


     Note Passwordless login with passkeys is a pilot or beta service that is subject to the Beta Services
     Terms at Agreements - Salesforce.com or a written Unified Pilot Agreement if executed by Customer,




                                                       838
Salesforce Release Notes                                                        Security, Identity, and Privacy



     and applicable terms in the Product Terms Directory. Use of this pilot or beta service is at the
     Customer's sole discretion.


Who: This feature is available only for internal users, such as employees, who log in to your Salesforce
org. It isn't available for Experience Cloud site users.

Why: Passkeys are phishing-resistant, making them more secure than password-based authentication.
They're also more convenient for users. Because passkeys inherently use multiple factors for
authentication, they satisfy the Salesforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) requirement. So, if users log
in with a passkey, they aren't prompted to provide a second factor for authentication, saving time and
effort with each login.

Passkeys are based on the Fast IDentity Online (FIDO) authentication standard. For more information on
the benefits of passkeys, see the FIDO documentation.

How: You can enable passwordless login with passkeys on the Identity Verification page in Setup.
Passwordless login with passkeys is available only for users with a registered built-in authenticator or
security key, and only for saved usernames. To log in, users click on their saved username and then use
their built-in authenticator or security key.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Passwordless Login with Passkeys (Beta) (can be outdated or unavailable during
  release preview)
  Salesforce Help: Enable Passwordless Login with Passkeys (Beta) (can be outdated or unavailable
  during release preview)

framework, which supports single sign-on (SSO) with only one identity provider. We’re giving you a final
reminder that with Summer ’26, we’re no longer supporting the single-configuration SAML framework. To

framework, which supports SSO with multiple identity providers instead of just one. If you don’t migrate,

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in

     Note This release update is available only if you’re using the single-configuration SAML framework. If

     this release update doesn’t apply to your instance.


When: This update is enforced for production instances in Summer ’26 and was enforced for sandboxes
in Summer ’24. To get the major release upgrade date for your instance, go to Trust Status, search for
your instance, and click the maintenance tab.

This update was first made available in Spring ’24. It was scheduled to be enforced for all instances in
Summer ’24, but we enforced it only for sandboxes in Summer ’24. We postponed the enforcement date
for production instances to Spring ’26 and then postponed it again to Summer ’26.

Why: We’re removing support for the single-configuration SAML SSO framework that you currently use.
With this change, all SAML SSO configurations must use our newer multiple-configuration framework.
With the multiple-configuration SAML framework, you can integrate your org or Experience Cloud site
with multiple external identity providers.

How: If you don’t migrate to the multiple-configuration SAML framework, your SAML SSO configuration
will break when this update is enforced.

When you follow the steps to migrate, your current SAML SSO configuration is preserved, but with some
key changes:


                                                   840
Salesforce Release Notes                                                         Security, Identity, and Privacy


• Your Salesforce login URL changes. Make sure you have a plan to communicate this change to your
    users.
• SAML responses from your identity provider must include the audience attribute. Work with your
    identity provider to update SAML responses as needed.
•   Salesforce generates a new self-signed certificate and uses it to sign SAML requests.
•   If Salesforce can’t parse a SAML response, it isn’t recorded in the login history.

Before you migrate your configuration in production, make sure you understand these changes, update
your configuration accordingly, and test all changes in a sandbox.

To review this update, from Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and then select

Triple DES for SAML Single Sign-On Stops Working in Summer ’26

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability



                                                   842
Salesforce Release Notes                                                        Security, Identity, and Privacy


within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

In Summer ’26, SAML single sign-on (SSO) configurations that use the Triple Data Encryption Standard
(Triple DES) algorithm will stop working. This change applies to all SSO configurations that use the Triple
DES algorithm, whether you use Salesforce as an identity provider or as a service provider. To improve
security, use the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithms, AES 128 or AES 256, instead.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in all
editions.

When: Triple DES will stop working in Summer ’26. There’s no change to Triple DES support in Spring ’26,
but we recommend that you update your SAML configurations as soon as possible.

Why: The Triple DES algorithm uses a cryptographic key that’s too short to be secure. The AES 128 and
AES 256 algorithms use longer keys that make these algorithms harder to attack. For more information
about encryption algorithm security from the National Institute of Standards and Technology, go to
https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/131/a/r3/ipd.

How: Before Summer ’26, update your configurations to use the AES 128 or AES 256 algorithm. The
steps to update your configuration are different depending on whether you use Salesforce as an identity
provider or as a service provider.

• If you use Salesforce as an identity provider, check your connected app SAML configuration. First, go to
  your connected app Web App Settings and check the Block Encryption Algorithm setting. If Block
  Encryption Algorithm is set to Triple DES, update your configuration to use a more secure algorithm.
  On the service provider, update your settings to decrypt the new algorithm.




• If you use Salesforce as a service provider, check with your identity provider to see what encryption
  algorithm they use. If they use the Triple DES algorithm, work with your identity provider to use a more
  secure algorithm and to generate a new decryption certificate. In Salesforce, update the Assertion
  Decryption Certificate in your SAML Single Sign-On Settings.




                                                    843
Salesforce Release Notes                                                       Security, Identity, and Privacy

  Salesforce Help: Configure SSO with Salesforce as a SAML Service Provider (can be outdated or
  unavailable during release preview)
  Salesforce Help: Salesforce as a SAML Identity Provider (can be outdated or unavailable during release
  preview)

Reduce friction in the encryption process with Database Encryption, now generally available in all
regions. Bring Your Own Key for Data 360 opens more root key management options.

  Encrypt Your Entire Database (GA Release)
  Database Encryption is generally available worldwide. It began its deployment in Winter '26. Due to
  the pace of the controlled release, some regions lagged in enabling the new feature. Database
  Encryption allows you to sort, filter and reference encrypted data without functional or performance
  tradeoffs. You can still apply Field Level Encryption to individual fields if required.
  Bring Your Own Key to Data 360
  Platform Encryption for Data 360 customers can now make use of the Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)
  feature of Shield Platform Encryption. When you supply your own root key, you get the benefits built
  into Salesforce Shield Platform Encryption, plus the extra assurance that comes from exclusively
  managing your own key material. For Data 360, BYOK supports root keys only. Data 360 then manages
  all DEK creation and wrapping using the root key. To be compatible with Salesforce BYOK, use a
  PKCS#8 encrypted, Base64 encoded 4096 RSA key pair with appropriate headers and footers.

Agentforce Service Assistant

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Expand the capabilities of Agentforce Service Assistant by adding the Case Feed and Messaging Session
and Voice Call records as grounding sources to improve service plan accuracy and relevance. We've also
added translation support, allowing service plans to be presented in the service rep's preferred language.

  Draft Service Plans in Service Rep's Preferred Language
  Have service reps work Cases faster using service plans that are translated into their preferred
  language. When service reps draft a service plan, the plan is generated in your company’s preferred
  language. Additionally, when have Real-Time Translations enabled, the service plan is then translated
  into the service rep's preferred language.
  Use Case Feed as the Latest Grounding Source to Strengthen Service Plans
  Adding Case Feed data to Service Assistant improves the accuracy and relevance of Service Plans. This
  richer, more contextual case activity enables the assistant to deliver more informed, relevant
  recommendations.
  Add More Context to Service Plans with Messaging Session and Voice Call Record Grounding
  Enhance the accuracy and details of service plans by grounding Service Assistant in Messaging Session
  and Voice Call records. When these records are attached to a case, Service Assistant analyzes the
  transcripts to create a case summary that summarizes what took place in the conversation and drafts a
  service plan that continues from where the conversation ended. The grounding process boosts rep
  productivity by ensuring the service plan continues exactly from where the prior interaction left off and
  avoids repeating steps and manual context gathering.
  Draft Comprehensive Service Plans with Expanded Data Access
  Service Assistant now drafts all service plans based on the permissions of the ServicePlanner User (the
  digital agent), rather than the individual service rep. This ensures that every service plan contains the
  most detailed information, regardless of an individual rep's field-level access or sharing rules.

Draft Service Plans in Service Rep's Preferred Language

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Have service reps work Cases faster using service plans that are translated into their preferred language.
When service reps draft a service plan, the plan is generated in your company’s preferred language.
Additionally, when have Real-Time Translations enabled, the service plan is then translated into the
service rep's preferred language.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

• Translation of service plans into your company’s default language is available with Einstein for Service,
    Agentforce for Service, and Agentforce 1 editions.
•   Translation of service plans into your service reps preferred language is available only with Agentforce
    for Service and Agentforce 1 editions.

Who:

• Translating and viewing service plans in your company’s preferred language is available for all users by
    default.
•   To turn on Real-Time Translations for Service Assistant, Salesforce admins need the Service Planner
    Builder permission set.
•   To view service plans in their preferred language, service reps need the Service Plan Translation and
    Service Plan User permission sets.

Why: Previously, service plans only supported English, which slowed down service reps who weren't
fluent in English. Now, service plans are translated to provide native-language clarity so service reps work
faster and efficiently. Specifically:

• Service Assistant automatically drafts service plans in your company's preferred language when the
    language is supported in Prompt Builder. See Supported Languages in Prompt Builder.
•   When the Real-Time Translations feature is turned on, Service Assistant translates service plans into
    your service reps’ preferred language. Service Assistant supports the same languages as Real Time
    Translations. See Real-Time Translations.




                                                     865
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                                Service




How:

• Translation of service plans into your company’s preferred language is automatically enabled. However,
  the language must be a part of the Prompt Builder supported languages.
• To turn on Real-Time Translations, go to the Real-Time Translations Setup page and turn on the feature
  for Service Assistant. After, assign your service reps the Service Plan Translation permission set.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Supported Languages in Prompt Template Responses (can be outdated or unavailable
  during release preview)

Add More Context to Service Plans with Messaging Session and Voice Call Record
Grounding

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Enhance the accuracy and details of service plans by grounding Service Assistant in Messaging Session
and Voice Call records. When these records are attached to a case, Service Assistant analyzes the
transcripts to create a case summary that summarizes what took place in the conversation and drafts a
service plan that continues from where the conversation ended. The grounding process boosts rep
productivity by ensuring the service plan continues exactly from where the prior interaction left off and
avoids repeating steps and manual context gathering.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Unlimited, and Developer editions
with Einstein for Service, Agentforce for Service, and Agentforce 1 editions.

When: This feature was originally released on December 18, 2025. We’ve included it in the Spring '26
Release Notes to increase the visibility of the feature.

Who:


                                                   868
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                             Service


• To set up Messaging Session and Voice Call record grounding for Service Assistant, Salesforce admins
    need the Service Planner Builder permission set.
• To ground service plans in Messaging Session or Voice Call records, the ServicePlanner User needs the
    Conversation Grounding Access custom permission set that has these permissions.
     - App permission: Access Conversations Entries, View All Voice and Video Calls
     - Messaging Session object permission: Read, View All Records
•   To view Messaging Session or Voice Call information in a service plan, service reps need the Service
    Planner User permission set.

Why: By automatically grounding the case summary and service plan in the related conversation
transcript, Service Assistant limits the need for service reps to manually review and synthesize the
Messing Session or Voice Call record. In addition, the service plan starts from where the original
conversation ended, which speeds up case resolution and prevents the duplication of resolution steps
already taken the conversation.




                                                    869
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                      Service




How: Assign your users the required permissions and then turn on Messaging and Voice record
grounding in the Case tab of the Service Assistant Setup page.

Draft Comprehensive Service Plans with Expanded Data Access

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Service Assistant now drafts all service plans based on the permissions of the ServicePlanner User (the
digital agent), rather than the individual service rep. This ensures that every service plan contains the
most detailed information, regardless of an individual rep's field-level access or sharing rules.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Unlimited, and Developer editions
with Einstein for Service, Agentforce for Service, and Agentforce 1 editions.

When: This feature was originally released on December 18, 2025. We’ve included it in the Spring '26
Release Notes to increase the visibility of the feature.

Who: This change applies to the ServicePlanner User and service reps.

Why: Previously, plans were drafted based on the service rep's permissions, which could limit the
inclusion of relevant data based on field-level access, object access, and sharing rules. For example, by
using the ServicePlanner User's permissions for plan generation:

• Service plans now include all fields and object information set in your Service AI Grounding
  configuration, even if the service rep doesn’t have field-level access.
• Plan steps are always grounded in your relevant knowledge articles, even when the service rep doesn’t
  have access to the articles used to create the plan.

How: The feature is enabled by default, so no action is required. However, you should review your
configurations for all grounding sources. To learn more about how permissions determine data access for
each Service Assistant feature, see Service Assistant Grounding Data Access.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Service Assistant Grounding Data Access
  Salesforce Help: Service Assistant Grounding Sources
  Salesforce Help: Service Assistant Permissions and Licensing

Gain Instant Case Context with Case Timeline

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available

where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability

Give your reps a single, unified, and intelligent timeline component for cases. This new component
replaces the current fragmented collection of feeds and related lists with a single curated view of case-
related events. Reps get instant context with a proactive workspace that intelligently organizes customer
conversations, internal team collaboration, and key case milestones. The new timeline brings together
channels like emails, chats, and messages into a clean, threaded view.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions where Industries Service Excellence is enabled.




                                                   873
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                                  Service


Why: Reps spend too much time navigating disparate systems and sifting through data to find critical
information, which causes information fatigue and slower resolution times. Without immediate insight
into case progress or historical data, it’s hard for reps to prioritize effectively and identify root causes. The
new timeline gives a scannable, easy-to-understand view of all activity. It visually distinguishes owner
changes, SLA breaches, and escalations as clearly marked milestones. Pre-configured Timeline Templates
are available immediately for use in the Timeline feature, requiring no configuration.

How: In Setup, in the Quick Find Box, find and select Timeline. In the Timeline window, turn on the

Easily View Original Case Attachments

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Reps can now view the original case attachments directly from the case details page. Original
attachments include any files added by the customer in the initial message at the time of case creation.
This feature eliminates the need for reps to navigate to the Attachments related list to locate these files.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Essentials, Professional, Enterprise, Performance,
Unlimited, and Developer editions.

Why: Reps can lose case context if they can’t view the attachments in the initial customer message. The
Attachments related List doesn’t distinguish between attachments added during case creation and those
added later. This feature makes it easier for reps to view the original attachments, improving case context
and productivity.

How: The feature is turned on by default and is visible to all reps who have access to the case record and
attachments. To turn it off, contact your Salesforce Customer Support.

On the Case Details page, click See Attachments to open the Original Attachments panel. To see all
attachments, click View All Attachments.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Case Feed and Related Lists


Enhance Your Security of Organization-Wide Email Addresses

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.



                                                    875
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                           Service


Organization-Wide Email Addresses (OWA) are now required to be verified before sending Case emails
with custom content. This security enhancement prevents unauthorized use of the
<noreply@salesforce.com> address and protects against potential phishing attempts.

Where: This change applies to all Salesforce editions that support Case email functionality.

Why: This security update ensures that all customers configure and verify their Organization-Wide Email
Address before sending Case emails containing custom content. Previously, some organizations could
bypass this requirement, creating a security risk where unauthorized users could potentially send
malicious emails using the trusted @salesforce.com domain. This enhancement closes that security gap
by enforcing verification requirements across all organizations.

How: If you've already configured and verified your Organization-Wide Email Address, no action is
needed. If you haven't set up your Organization-Wide Email Address or if your current setup wasn't
previously enforced, you must configure a verified Organization-Wide Email Address before sending
emails with custom content. For setup instructions, see Set Up Organization-Wide Email Addresses in
Salesforce Help.

Enhancements include new and updated features for Service Email.

  Email Across Languages with Real-Time Translations
  Let service reps translate Service Email conversations, expanding customer support across languages.
  A rep can translate an end user’s email into the rep’s language, as well as translate their response into
  the end user’s language before sending. Previously, a Service Email rep had to speak the same
  language as an end user in order to assist.
  Agent Session Continuity is Improved for Case-Related Email Threads
  An Agentforce Agent session now remains associated with a case and all of its related emails over a
  three-day period. This preserves crucial information and context variables, such as user verification
  status or variables set by previous actions. Previously, a new session was opened for every inbound
  email, causing AI to lose conversation history and requiring repeated reinterpretation of earlier
  interactions.
  Inbound Limit for Service Agent Emails is Extended
  Inbound emails handled by the Service agent count against your Agentforce for Service on Email daily
  transaction limit, which is 5,000 by default. You can ask Salesforce Customer Support to raise this
  limit. Previously, this checked against the org's single email limit, which is shared with Apex and flow
  emails.
  Email Composer is Modernized with New Button Colors
  As part of a TinyMCE upgrade, the email composer button icons changed from grey to blue. This
  brings the composer up to our Salesforce Lightning Design System standards.

Review De-Duplication Activity for Unified WhatsApp

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

New logic ensures that you contact the most recently added individual in a Unified WhatsApp channel,
and new error codes explain why other duplicate individuals weren’t contacted. Previously, there wasn’t
logic to choose an Individual, and there weren’t error codes to explain why we made the choice.

Where: This change applies to Unified WhatsApp in Enterprise and Unlimited editions for Marketing


                                                   885
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                             Service


Cloud Engagement Growth and Advanced Editions.

Why: If a Unified Individual has multiple associated individuals, each with the same phone number, we
only contact one Individual. We chose the latest Individual that was created with that phone number.

We introduced three new error codes to help explain why an individual wasn’t contacted.

• SF-3025 - The message wasn't sent because the recipient's phone number wasn't a valid E.164
    number. Correct the phone number and try again.
•   SF-3045 - The message wasn't sent because the recipient's phone number is associated with a
    different individual ID.
•   SF-3035 - The message wasn't sent because a contact record wasn't found.

How: To view the Individuals associated with a Unified Individual, and to see error messages explaining
which Individuals were or weren’t contacted, create a Data Cloud Data Explorer view. For a Data Lake
Object view, add the Error Code and Not Sent Reason columns. For a Data Model Object view, add the
Messaging Error Code and Error Message columns.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: WhatsApp Engagement Data in Unified Messaging

Maintain Service for Your Bring Your Own Channel Integration by Migrating Settings Fields

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.




                                                   887
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                              Service


To improve the scalability of Bring Your Own Channel messaging services, we implemented changes to
event-driven settings fields in the ConversationChannelDefinition and CustomMsgChannel objects. New
fields are available in Winter ’26 (API version 65.0), and old fields are removed in Spring ’26 (API version
66.0). These are breaking changes.

Where: This change applies to Bring Your Own Channel for Messaging and Bring Your Own Channel for
CCaaS. View required editions.

Who: These changes impact partners who create messaging provider integrations for Bring Your Own
Channel for Messaging or Bring Your Own Channel for CCaaS and customers who have self-implemented
Bring Your Own Channel for Messaging. These changes also impact customers using partner-provided
managed packages with removed fields. Customers must update their managed package to one that
contains supported fields by Spring ’26.

How: Learn more about the removed event-driven settings fields and assess whether your
implementation requires updates to migrate to their replacements. Make required changes by Spring
’26, when the fields will be removed.

• For ConversationChannelDefinition, deprecated fields are IsInboundReceiptsEnabled,
    IsRoutingWorkResultEnabled, and IsTypingIndicatorDisabled.
     - Use EventCapabilitiesIsInboundAcknwOptionExposed instead of IsInboundReceiptsEnabled.
     - Use EventCapabilitiesIsRoutingWorkResultSupported instead of IsRoutingWorkResultEnabled.
     - Use EventCapabilitiesIsTypingIndicatorOptionHidden instead of IsTypingIndicatorDisabled.
•   For CustomMsgChannel, deprecated fields are HasInboundReceipts and HasTypingIndicator.
     - Use EventCapabilitiesIsInboundAcknowledgementEnabled instead of HasInboundReceipts.
     - Use EventCapabilitiesIsTypingIndicatorDisabled instead of HasTypingIndicator.
If you don’t make required updates by Spring ’26 or if customers use a managed package version with
removed fields starting in Spring ’26, your implementation will break.

See Also
  Object Reference for the Salesforce Platform: ConversationChannelDefinition
  Salesforce Metadata API Developer Guide: ConversationChannelDefinition
  Salesforce Tooling API Guide: ConversationChannelDefinition
  Object Reference for the Salesforce Platform: CustomMsgChannel
  Salesforce Tooling API Guide: CustomMsgChannel


Voice

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability

                                                    888
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                              Service


Explore the latest Service Cloud Voice enhancements that empower reps and supervisors to more
efficiently and effectively resolve customer issues over the phone.

  Scale Your VoiceCall Object with More Custom Fields
  For greater flexibility, the maximum number of custom fields for the standard VoiceCall object is
  increased to 300. This update improves data capacity and avoids the architectural complexity of
  creating custom objects or polling other standard objects to store voice-related data.
  Manage Contact Center Groups and Queues in Bulk
  Save time and reduce manual data entry when managing your contact center. Admins can now use
  the Bulk API to create contact center groups and queues in bulk. This enhancement improves admin
  efficiency, supports large contact centers, and enables more comprehensive data management.
  Add Flexibility to Unified Routing Transfers by Routing Calls to a Flow
  Simplify the decision process for your reps by configuring voice call transfers with Omni-Channel
  Flows. This Omni-Channel Unified Routing enhancement unlocks more dynamic routing capabilities,
  allowing you to use complex business logic and skill-based criteria within a flow to determine the next
  transfer target.
  Route Voicemails and Desk Phone Calls with Unified Routing
  Unified Routing now supports voicemails and desk phone calls. This feature reduces wait times,
  improves rep productivity, and provides an efficient Omni-Channel experience. You can use this
  feature only if your telephony provider supports it.
  Minimize Abandoned Calls with Queued Callbacks for Omni-Channel Unified Routing
  Respect customers’ time, save telephony minutes, and keep callers from abandoning their calls by
  giving them the option to request a callback without losing their place in a queue. When a rep accepts
  a contact request in Omni-Channel, an outbound call to the customer starts automatically. The initial
  inbound call, contact request, and outbound call are all linked for easy rep reference. This feature is
  available for contact centers using Omni-Channel Unified Routing.
  Use Voicemail Drop for Outbound Calls (Beta)
  When an outbound call reaches voicemail, you can disconnect the call to automatically leave your
  default pre-recorded message. While the system plays the message, you can move on to your next task
  immediately, increasing your productivity. You can record multiple messages and select one as your
  default.
  Link Voice Calls to Their Source Records Automatically
  When you initiate an outbound call by using Click-to-Dial from a custom object, or a contact role on a
  Case or Opportunity, the resulting VoiceCall record now automatically establishes a lookup
  relationship to the source record. This change removes the need for manual linking and reduces the
  need for customization with Flows or Apex triggers. Previously, this automatic linking was available
  only for Account, Case, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, CollectionPlan, and ContactRequest records.
  Get Actionable Error Messages for Failed Outbound Calls
  When an outbound call fails to connect, reps now have descriptive and actionable error messages
  directly in the Omni-Channel widget, which helps them to take immediate corrective action. This
  feature improves rep productivity and helps increase successful call connection rates.
  Get the Latest Enhancements for Your Amazon Connect Contact Center
  Update your contact center to version 20.0 to unlock the latest Service Cloud Voice features. This



                                                  889
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                           Service


  version introduces a Lambda layer for running service health checks, and contact flows and subflows
  for voicemail drop. To test the updates before they go live in production, deploy them to your sandbox
  first.
  Update Your United States AWS Billing Address for Accurate Emergency Calling Fees
  As of March 1, 2025, AWS charges emergency calling fees for Amazon Connect based on the
  subaccount billing address. By default, Salesforce uses its own address for Service Cloud Voice with
  Amazon Connect customers with companies in the United States. To ensure correct charges and
  compliance with local regulations, update your AWS account to reflect your company’s address
  instead.

  Improve SLA Reporting by Using Rule-based Milestone Pause
  Free up your service reps from the manual overhead of stopping a record when the next step is
  outside their purview. Admins can set rules to automatically pause milestones when the defined
  conditions are met. For example, a milestone can be paused automatically if the case status is
  “Waiting for Customer.” The milestone timer stops during the pause duration and resumes when the
  pause conditions change. The target date is reevaluated when the milestone unpauses. This helps with
  more accurate SLA reporting and clearly highlights delays.

  targets, and see which records are close to missing an SLA.

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available

With the improved Lightning Article Editor, write knowledge articles more efficiently. Take advantage of
the streamlined features to create top-notch content.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Essentials, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
and Developer editions.

How: To help you write knowledge articles more efficiently, Lightning Article Editor has several key
improvements.

Here are the general improvements.

• You can now use Dark Mode in the article editor, making it easier to edit content in low-light
    environments.
•   Editing articles on the iPad is now easier. The expanded toolbar in narrow layouts no longer blocks
    your editing space, allowing full access to toolbar options while you edit.



                                                    916
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                              Service


• The editor toolbar is now visually consistent. Split buttons now match the size and look of the other
    buttons.
• You can now edit smart links in bulleted or numbered lists in knowledge articles without affecting the
    formatting of the list.
•   You can now easily switch between numeric (1, 2, 3) and alphabetic (a, b, c) numbering styles in
    nested lists. Previously, switching from alphabetic back to numeric wasn't easy.
•   We've resolved general formatting issues with numbered and bulleted lists in the article editor.
•   The format and alignment of bulleted lists are now the same in the draft version and the published
    article.
•   The paragraph spacing is now consistent in the article editor and accurately reflects the spacing in the
    published article.
•   Anchor links in Knowledge articles now smoothly scroll to the target section, giving readers a better
    experience in long articles.
•   In Chromium browsers like Chrome, Edge, Opera, and Brave, dragging content in the article editor
    caused unexpected scrolling. This issue is now fixed, making drag-and-drop much better.
• The tooltips on toolbar buttons now disappear as expected when you move your mouse away.
Here are the accessibility-related improvements.

• Screen reader users can now give article feedback more easily. Screen readers correctly announce
    “Was this article helpful?” when they reach the Like or Dislike buttons on the article.
•   We increased the contrast ratio for non-text elements like icons, buttons, and borders in the article
    editor to meet accessibility standards, making the interface easier to use for users with low-vision.
•   The article editor now shows the word count and includes ARIA label, making it easy for screen reader
    users to track their word count as they write.

Bill AI Self-Service Usage More Accurately with Session-Based Tracking

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability

Get more accurate billing for AI powered Self Service activity by tracking usage per authenticated login
session.This feature groups all AI interactions, like Knowledge Article Summary or Dynamic Q&A within a
single session, providing usage reports that reflect how customers engage with Agentic Portal features.



                                                    923
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                             Service


Where: This change applies to Aura or LWR sites accessed through Lightning Experience and Salesforce
Classic in Enterprise, Professional, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

Who: This feature is available to authenticated users working in orgs that use Customer Community,
Customer Community Plus, Customer Community Login, Customer Community Plus Login, and the
corresponding unlimited login variants. Users must have access to Agentic Portal capabilities, including
AI Knowledge Article Summary and Dynamic Q&A.

Why: Agentic Portals introduce AI-driven features that are often used together in a single visit. Tracking
usage at the session level gives you clearer consumption data, reduces noise in billing reports, and aligns
with the broader Self-Service monetization strategy. You get transparent usage records, easier auditing,
and greater accuracy when customers operate within contractual AI usage limits.

How: Session based usage tracking records AI feature activity for each authenticated login session.
During a session, all AI interactions are collected and combined into a single usage record. Billing entries
are created on a daily or configurable schedule and include session details and aggregated activity. Usage
logs and reports provide visibility into feature consumption.


Improve Dynamic Q&A Performance with Persisted Questions and Answers
for Authenticated Users

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Dynamic Q&A now loads faster and reduces Large Language Model (LLM) calls by persisting generated
questions and answers for authenticated users. Previously, Dynamic Q&A regenerated a new set of
questions each time an authenticated user viewed an article. The feature now stores the generated
questions, which improves performance and gives users quicker access to relevant answers.

Where: This change applies to Aura or LWR sites accessed through Lightning Experience and Salesforce
Classic in Enterprise, Professional, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

Who: Available to authenticated Experience Cloud users with Customer Community or Customer
Community Plus licenses. Also available to internal users with a Knowledge license when accessing
knowledge-related features. Experience Cloud site builders need permissions to add and configure the
Dynamic Q&A component in Experience Builder.

Why: In the previous release, Dynamic Q&A persisted questions and answers only for guest users.
Authenticated users received newly generated questions on every request, which required repeated calls
to the large language model and increased latency. With this enhancement, Dynamic Q&A now persists
generated questions for authenticated users as well, which reduces repeated processing, lowers overall



                                                    924
Salesforce Release Notes                                                                              Service


Large Language Model (LLM) usage, and delivers faster article-level answers.

How: Dynamic Q&A now stores the generated set of questions and answers for authenticated users.
When a user returns to the same article, the component shows the persisted questions instead of
generating new ones. This reduces load times and avoids repeated calls to the Large Language Model
(LLM). Component behavior and configuration in Experience Builder remain unchanged.


Monitor Proactive Service Campaign Performance

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Gain a unified view of your service campaign performance with the campaign analytics dashboard. You
can monitor outreach, open rates, completion rates, bounce rates, and individual customer progress to
assess campaign health and week-over-week trends. Use these insights to identify issues, follow up with
customers, and measure campaign return on investment (ROI).

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Unlimited, and Developer editions of
Service Cloud.

Who: To create the app, you need the Data Cloud admin permission sets, Tableau Limited Viewer license
and permission sets, and Service cloud data kit.

Route Voice Conversations to External Bots

This release is in preview

Note: This release is in preview. Features described in this document don't become generally available
until the latest general availability date that Salesforce announces for this release. Before then, and
where features are noted as beta, pilot, or developer preview, we can't guarantee general availability
within any particular time frame or at all. Make your purchase decisions only on the basis of generally
available products and features.

Route voice conversations to your preferred external bots by using the Route Work action in Omni-
Channel flows. You can use external bots that are tailored to your specific needs and preferences.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions where Service Cloud Voice and Agentforce
are enabled.

Why: AI agents answer questions 24/7, reducing wait times and improving accessibility for customers. AI
agents handle frequently asked questions, enabling service reps to focus on more complex tasks.
Integrate external bots, such as Google CCAI, and customize them to meet your specific business
requirements.

How: In Setup, in the Quick Find box, find and select Flows. Select a flow or click New Flow to create a
new flow. In Flow Builder, add Route Work action to the canvas. In the Route Work action, select Phone



                                                   927
Salesforce Release Notes                                              Other Salesforce Products and Services


as the Service Channel. In the Route To field, select External Conversation Bot, and then select the AI
agent’s name in the External Conversation Bot field.
